task.goal: A binary RPC server receives 4-byte big-endian length-prefixed messages in arbitrary chunks. FrameDecoder.feed currently parses each chunk independently and can lose a partial prefix or body; it also accepts frames larger than max_size. Fix FrameDecoder in framing.py so feed returns only complete frames, keeps partial bytes for later calls, handles several frames per chunk, rejects oversized lengths before buffering the body, and can continue after a complete frame. Run tests and validate.

result.text:
I'll start by inspecting the repository structure and the framing module.Now I'll add tests covering the required behaviors and run them.Fixed `FrameDecoder` in framing.py: `feed` now appends each chunk to an internal `bytearray` buffer, parses headers from the buffer, buffers partial prefixes/bodies for later calls, returns all complete frames from a chunk, and raises `ValueError` when a declared length exceeds `max_size` before reading the body. Decoder state persists across calls, so it continues after complete frames.

Added coverage in test_framing.py for multi-frame chunks, partial prefix, partial body, byte-at-a-time delivery, continuation across calls, oversized rejection, and boundary `max_size`. `python3 -m unittest -v test_framing` passes all 9 tests (validated, exit 0). Nothing left unverified.
